clue.text: Having made a mistake, hesitate with embarrassment

parts.note: er is the sound a speaker makes when hesitating
embarrassment makes the face go red

explanation.surface: Someone who has slipped up falters, blushing.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to go wrong, so the past form describes someone who has blundered.

clue.text: Stamp the thirteenth letter placed before the manager

indicators.note: the letter's name is set ahead of the next piece in the answer

parts.note: M, the thirteenth letter of the alphabet, is spelt out as em
a boss is the person in charge, a manager

explanation.surface: Instructions for franking a letter M in front of the person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To emboss is to press a raised design into a surface, as a stamp or seal does.

clue.text: Catalogue of neckwear accessories as evidence of breeding

explanation.surface: A list of collar fittings that somehow proves good pedigree.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the first half is a book of collar studs, the small fasteners once used to attach detachable shirt collars.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud register records the pedigrees of horses or other animals, so it documents bloodlines; the first reading jokingly takes it as a list of collar fasteners.

clue.text: Additional neckwear a Pole cuts out

parts.note: S stands for the South Pole
to carve is to cut out a shape

explanation.surface: A Polish tailor snips out extra neck garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality; it is the geographical pole, S. 'Additional' links this neckwear to that of the clue before.
explanation.definitionFit: Woollen wraps worn round the throat are a further kind of neck garment after the collar studs.

clue.text: Try either side of a waistcoat for a bit of burlesque

indicators.note: the word Try is split so that its letters sit on both sides of what follows

parts.note: vest is a word for waistcoat, especially in American usage

explanation.surface: Advice to try on a waistcoat from both sides for a comic stage turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like the verb inviting you to sample a garment; it is fodder split around the rest by 'either side of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotesque parody or mockery is the stuff of burlesque, which ridicules by exaggerated imitation.

clue.text: Outlandish bird lured by a hawker

explanation.surface: A strange bird is tempted down by a falconer.
explanation.walkthrough: A hawker here is a falconer, one who hunts with hawks, not a street seller.
explanation.definitionFit: The word's old sense is foreign or alien, and it also names the falcon prized in falconry, recalled to the lure.

clue.text: Leg of bird which is tattooed

explanation.surface: A chicken leg that has been inked.
explanation.walkthrough: A tattoo is also a drum beat or military display, so the stick 'tattoos' the drum.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower leg of a cooked fowl shares its name with the stick that beats out a rhythm on a drum.

clue.text: Work for a barrister economical with words

explanation.surface: A terse lawyer's assignment.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister's instructions in a case are this, and the same word means short and concise.

clue.text: A case to take firmly in hand

explanation.surface: Picking up a suitcase with a firm hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling bag or holdall is an old name for this, and the verb means to clutch tightly.

clue.text: And a judge who has things taped

explanation.surface: Following on from the barrister, a judge who has everything under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has things taped' sounds like 'has things under control' but means a tape machine. 'And' links back to the barrister in the clue before.
explanation.definitionFit: In England a part-time circuit judge holds this title, and a tape machine that stores sound is named the same.

clue.text: Variety performance to see again

explanation.surface: Going back to watch a variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense uses an older spelling of revue, a show of sketches, songs and dances.
explanation.definitionFit: A song-and-sketch show has been spelt this way, and the verb also means to look over a second time.

clue.text: Capital solo arrangement

indicators.note: a musical arrangement here signals that the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A solo piece arranged in a major city.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway's seat of government is a capital city.

clue.text: Major exhibition certain to provide a film shot

parts.note: an expo is a large trade or world fair
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A big show guaranteed to provide a good photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Each frame of a camera roll is a single exposed image, one photograph's worth of light on the emulsion.

clue.text: On which men who were detained once walked to work

definitions.text: On which men who were detained once walked to work

parts.words: On which men who were detained once walked to work
parts.note: Victorian prisoners trudged on a wheel of steps that turned machinery; read loosely it suggests a commuter's route

explanation.surface: A description of how prisoners of old went about their labour.
explanation.walkthrough: Victorian prisons punished inmates by making them tread a large stepped wheel, often grinding corn.
explanation.definitionFit: The prison wheel was a penal device, and the word now means any monotonous routine of toil.

clue.text: Goad is all right when going in to raise dough

indicators.note: the letters for all right are placed inside the baking word

parts.note: to prove dough is to let it rise before baking
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A baker says it is fine to step in and let the bread rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To goad someone is to needle or incite them into a reaction.

clue.text: Vacation-but O for a job!

indicators.note: an O is put in place of one letter, here the first A of the holiday word

explanation.surface: Someone wishing their holiday were a paid post instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first A of VACATION for O.
explanation.definitionFit: A calling or profession is a line of work.

clue.text: Make a song about a Scottish river while holidaying

indicators.note: the singing word goes round the river's name

parts.note: to make a song is to sing
the Tay is Scotland's longest river

explanation.surface: Composing a tune about the Tay while on a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a visit somewhere, lodging away from home, is a way of spending a holiday.

clue.text: Civil wrong sure to develop into judicial abuses

parts.note: a tort is a wrong in civil law, such as negligence

indicators.note: the word sure is to be reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: A legal injustice set to escalate into court cruelty.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically courts sanctioned inflicted pain, such as the rack, to extract confessions.

clue.text: Draw out what should be a short passage

explanation.surface: Pulling out what is meant to be a brief excerpt.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull something free and a short quoted passage from a book share this word.

clue.text: The big fight with striking possibilities?

definitions.text: The big fight with striking possibilities?

parts.words: The big fight with striking possibilities?
parts.note: read as boxing, a major bout full of punches; read literally, a small container whose contents are struck to light

explanation.surface: A heavyweight bout promising plenty of punches.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as a sports match plus box, as in boxing; the striking is of matches, not opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: A small case holds sticks struck to produce a flame, while the parts suggest a boxing contest.

clue.text: Juveniles in the club oyster bar

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across the words that follow

explanation.surface: Young people in the club's seafood bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Young males, lads, are juveniles.

clue.text: Raise the back

explanation.surface: Lifting up the rear end.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up children or lift up is one sense; the hind part of something is the other.

clue.text: Died in a fog — in the middle of it

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed inside the words that follow

parts.note: mist is a thin fog

explanation.surface: Someone perished lost in a fog.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means surrounded by or among, at the centre of things.

clue.text: Deposit ashes in their traditional depositary

parts.note: cremation ashes are traditionally kept in an urn

explanation.surface: Advice on where to place a loved one's ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: To place cremated remains in a vessel is the verb's meaning.

clue.text: Tim backward in not coming forward as a forger

indicators.note: the turned name goes inside the word for not coming forward

parts.note: shy people do not come forward

indicators.note: the name Tim is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Timid Tim, backward and reticent, is exposed as a counterfeiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns TIM into MIT. A forger here is one who forges metal, a blacksmith, not a counterfeiter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, usually a smith's workshop, is also used for the smith himself, who forges iron at the anvil.

clue.text: One's ruin is wrought by rallies

indicators.note: wrought means worked or shaped, so the letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: A person's downfall brought about by mass gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: Gatherings that bring people together again are rallies of old friends or comrades.

clue.text: What the speaker takes to stand on

explanation.surface: A question about where a public speaker stands.
explanation.walkthrough: A speaker 'takes the floor' to address a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the right to address a debate is to take this, and it is also the ground surface of a room.

clue.text: Admission by Roy involved with a crime?

parts.note: access is admission or entry

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters of the name are mixed up

explanation.surface: Roy's confession implicating himself in an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' turns ROY into ORY. The question mark flags the loose definition: one who is with a crime is party to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who aids a wrongdoer is an accomplice, linked with the offence.
